features.name: Chat
features.note: Checked live on the owner's account in W1.

features.name: Switching tool inside a chat
features.note: Opens a new chat beside the old one after one confirm. The text goes to the other vendor.

features.name: Several accounts, limit switch
features.note: Automatic moves between tools stay off.

features.name: Brain, recall, task log
features.note: Runs the same hooks. In a chat the write gate on marketing tokens and agent files works only after `dreamcontext install --tool codex --global`, one approval for the whole Mac. It covers file edits, not a shell command that writes those files. The live check is the owner's.

features.name: Skills (ours, the project's, the owner's)
features.note: No project step, nothing in `~/.codex`: copied to `~/.dreamcontext/codex` in Codex's words and listed through the app-server's extra skill roots. Live 2026-11-02 on one account: a fresh chat listed them, opened the dreamcontext skill and ran `tasks log` and `memory recall` unprompted.

features.name: Sub-agents (Claude's agents as Codex roles)
features.note: Ours, `~/.claude/agents` and the project's `.claude/agents` become roles for `spawn_agent`. Live 2026-11-02: `dreamcontext-explore` ran as a Codex sub-agent and answered. Other roles share the same path but were not each run live.

features.name: AI Team as chat sub-agents
features.note: A Codex pane gets no `--agents` and is not told about them.

features.name: Automations
features.note: No home board, no task steps. Sandboxed with no network, so a job that needs the web stays on Claude. Runs only after `dreamcontext install --tool codex` and trusting the folder and its hooks in Codex, which is what keeps writes off `_dream_context/marketing/.env` and agent files. Reading a `.env` is open, as on Claude. The approval question after an edit is asked on Codex too, read-only, never on Claude's account. Not run on a real Codex account yet.

features.name: AI Team agents
features.note: Same limits as automations. Changing the tool asks for approval again. Its own chat tab is not on Codex yet.

features.name: Super Agent
features.note: The lead stays on Claude: its verbs are off the brain MCP on purpose.

features.name: Super Agent's delegated child
features.note: `super delegate --tool codex`. stdio MCP servers only, and the same write gate as automations.

features.name: Terminal
features.note: `codex` on the chat's account, always workspace-write.

features.name: Sleep
features.note: `sleep auto-run --tool codex`, and a Codex chat's own auto sleep and Sleep now run on Codex. The cycle text names spawn_agent for the specialists. No live run recorded yet: the only free account hit its limit on 2 Nov.

features.name: Ask another tool (`dreamcontext ask`)
features.note: `dreamcontext ask --tool claude|codex|antigravity [--agent <role>] "<prompt>"`, read-only unless `--write`. Real turns 2 Nov: Claude asked Codex read-only (it read the project and answered) and with `--write` (it wrote in the project). Codex asking Claude was not proved: the free Codex account hit its limit first. A sandboxed Codex chat cannot hand a write to Claude or Antigravity. Antigravity: fake agent only, no real turn.

features.name: Develop builders, goal-skill, council on Codex and Antigravity
features.note: A Codex or Antigravity chat runs a skill's `claude -p` sessions as its own sub-agents (spawn_agent, invoke_subagent) and never starts `claude`. Codex threads fork (a real turn, 2 Nov), but the Develop fan-out runner starts Claude only: a Codex lead builds its waves itself. Not proved on a real goal-skill run.

features.name: Antigravity chat
features.note: Experimental, proved with real turns on one account (agent 1.4.1): sign-in, memory, approval cards, resume, skills listed and read from the account's profile, the brain MCP server, its identity. The write gate is the agent's own PreToolUse hook in each account's profile: real turns refused shell and file-tool writes to marketing tokens, in every mode and inside the agent's own sub-agents, and a project's .agents/hooks.json cannot switch it off. A Super child runs with `super delegate --tool antigravity`: no card, no child without the gate, `super read` returns its words. It has no OS sandbox, so a child or a Bypass agent can write outside the project. Stop reads the agent's conversation file, so sleep sees the turns. Our sub-agent roles (ours, the skill packs' and the owner's `~/.claude/agents`) are a plugin in each account's profile, called with `invoke_subagent`, refreshed as a chat opens and by the project catch-up; a project's own `.claude/agents` role is made with `define_subagent` from its file. Files and tests only, no real turn: the account is out of quota until about 8 Nov. The owner's tool servers reach its chats, and Settings > Tool servers shows what a live session reports: a server is asked first and left out if it does not answer, because one bad server refuses every turn of a session, and a server that wants a sign-in stays out because the agent has none. `sleep auto-run --tool antigravity` and Sleep now run on it, and so do automations and AI Team agents set to Antigravity (their approval question, a verdict's resume and peer delivery too); fake agent only, no real turn. Usage counts its tokens from those transcripts, with no price. Terminal stays off; a home board and a task step stay on Claude. Eco and account moves are proved against a fake agent only, and compaction was never reached on a real turn: the server refused past about 1M tokens. Context rides in the user's message, because ACP has no untrusted channel. OpenCode was dropped by the owner.
